knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Value for money is judged on whole-of-life cost and fit for the stated need, with non-financial factors also weighed. Purchase price alone ignores running and exit costs, and brand reputation is not a measure of the outcome.

Costs of moving to another supplier when the arrangement ends are a transition-out cost, which the rules list as an example of whole-of-life cost. A one-off discount reduces the price but is not an ongoing cost, and a supplier's own sales commission is not a buyer cost.

Value analysis starts with the function an element performs. The feature is removed or changed only once the outcome is confirmed to hold without it. Removing it immediately risks failure, and keeping it without review ignores the cost.

One-off switching costs such as training and a trial period are part of the cost of the change, so they must be counted against the benefits. Leaving out the benefits or the costs, or looking only at the unit price, gives a one-sided result.

practicalCriteria: Learner compares two written offers for the same specification on whole-of-life cost, with one-off, running and exit costs listed or marked not applicable with a reason. Pass: every cost category is addressed, and the result is stated in dollars over a stated period.
Learner labels every estimate as an assumption with its source or basis. Pass: no estimate appears without a label and a source or basis.
Learner records one non-financial factor on which the offers differ, and states how it was weighed in the decision. Pass: the factor is recorded and the decision record refers to it.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks. A quiz pass is not verified practical competence; the assessor signs off the practical criteria separately.
evidenceRequired: Whole-of-life or cost-benefit worksheet with dates, assumptions and sources
Decision record with value-for-money reasons, non-financial factors and review date
Assessor record of knowledge check result
Assessor sign-off against the three practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: Learner presents the lowest price as value for money without a whole-of-life comparison
Learner removes a feature from a specification without confirming the function it performs
Learner treats the 14 December 2020 landing-page version, the 2025 instrument, or tax treatment as settled without checking them
